doc.title: Larry Ridley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 10, 2003

title: Churning out clones, humility, Ph.D.s and tenure
summary: Teaching programs must foster personal identity; he mocks degrees and tenure complacency.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Well that’s why I think that people like myself and I have other people who are disciples like I am in recognizing how this can be a problem. And it’s true in anything. You can always find that you’re churning out clones as opposed to individualists. And we have to constantly check ourselves. And the people who are teaching and some of these degree programs need to make sure that they are structuring their curricula and their degree requirements so that you do produce people of substance and that you do produce people who recognize that they are searching for their own personal identity. Because it’s a lifelong quest. You know four years in an institution of higher yearning — I mean higher learning excuse me — that’s just preparing — you know there are a lot of people that come out and say oh I’m doctor so-and-so, I have a Ph.D. I say well what does that Ph.D. mean? Piled higher and deeper? And in what? So don’t get carried away because you’ve got a little Ph.D. behind your name. That doesn’t mean anything. You can find a person on the street with mother or father that can wipe you out so don’t get carried away. Put your ego in your back pocket and sit on it. And just recognize that you are a fellow human being and you are never in the position where you can look down your nose at anyone about anything. And once you lose your humility and we’re just like — you know how roaches are? You know we’re just one roach out of thousands of roaches. We are a microcosm of the macrocosm. And so people get — and I realize that everybody is searching for self identity and all these things and they’re searching for — they want to be comfortable, they want to find their own niche and everybody wants it to happen immediately. But I think it’s very important that as you are striving for these things that you are approaching it with the right criteria of understanding how to approach it. It’s not like I’m going to grab this. It’s just like the whole problem with academia with people going for tenure. They work their butts off while they’re trying to get tenure and many of them the minute they get tenure, whew.
Okay I can stop learning now.

And that’s what creates the controversy about tenure. Because you get so many people who do that. They work their butts off to get tenure and the minute they get tenure then they’re sitting on their asses for the rest of their life and trying to act like well I’m professor doctor so-and-so. So what? That and a dime ain’t going to get you on the subway in New York or anywhere else for that matter. So what? Like Miles said, so what? It don’t mean a thing if it ain’t got that swing.
